content: Firestore listeners deliver an initial snapshot from the local cache and then server data, so a component that renders before the first snapshot shows nothing unless an explicit loading state exists; the first query snapshot contains 'added' events for every existing document, so empty states must distinguish 'not loaded yet' from 'loaded and empty'. Firestore listen callbacks should always supply the error callback (permission-denied, invalid query) - after an error the listener receives no more events and does not need detaching. Community threads on React responsive tables (muhimasri, w3schools, Reddit r/webdev) converge on wrapping wide tables in an overflow-x: auto container with a visible scroll affordance, since a bare <table> forces the whole page to scroll horizontally on phones.
